title: Are Spring beans thread-safe?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Spring does not make beans thread-safe. A singleton bean is shared by all request threads, so any mutable instance field is a shared state bug. Most service and controller beans are stateless, holding only injected dependencies, so they are safe in practice. A bean with mutable fields needs synchronisation, a new bean per use, or thread-safe types. Don't store request data in a singleton's fields.

points.title: Singleton state
points.why: One singleton serves all threads, so mutable fields are shared between requests.

points.title: Stateless design
points.why: Beans that only hold dependencies are safe. Keep request data in method locals or request scope.
